content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper focuses on the MultiHiertt task, which involves answering questions that often require numerical reasoning over tables and text. The current paper extends previous work with a new program generator for those examples that require numerical reasoning. Questions that can be answered using span extraction are handled using a separate decoder, following previous work.

The program generator consists of several steps: program length prediction; operand identification; operator identification. These are sufficient to fill out program templates in the MultiHiertt format, which defines programs using 7 binary mathematical operators and variable ids to chain together results of sequential operations. The program generator is trained with direct supervision from the MultiHiertt annotations.

The new non-autoregressive approach is built upon the RoBERTA pretrained transformer language model. It significantly outperforms an autoregressive program generator baseline on the MultiHiertt task, that uses a LSTM decoder. The new method is also significantly faster than the LSTM baseline, as it doesn't require autoregressive decoding and can be run in a single forward pass through a transformer. Interestingly, the improvement in performance is more pronounced for text-only questions than for table-only questions.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
#### Strengths
- New method of program prediction that works very well on MultiHiertt, compared to autoregressive LSTM decoder.

#### Weaknesses
- This paper's contribution focuses on program generation for numerical reasoning. That contribution could also be applied to other tasks outside of the joint table and text MultiHiertt dataset. The paper would be stronger with a discussion of related numerical reasoning tasks (e.g. DROP for text, or semantic parsing over tables).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
#### Clarity
I found the paper hard to follow until I had familiarised myself with the MultiHiertt task, and the supervision available from that dataset. I suggest that some of the examples from Table 5 are moved from the appendix to the main text. Also the paper should explicitly describe the supervision available in MultiHiertt when describing the training of all modules in Section 3.2.

#### Novelty
I believe this is a novel method for the MultiHiertt dataset, which requires reasoning over both tables and text. However, given that the contributions are in the program generation module, I would be interested to see more comparison to other methods of program generation for other tasks that require numerical reasoning over either text (e.g. DROP) or tables.

#### Reproducability
The approach is reasonably straightforward and should be reproducable.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper presents a new numerical reasoning module to an existing system that can answer span-extraction or numerical-reasoning questions from evidence in text or tables. The new module targets the types of programs required to answer numerical reasoning questions in the MultiHiertt dataset, and it performs significantly better than the previous state of the art, which relied on an LSTM decoder.

The program prediction method is a nice addition to the MultiHiertt-focused system. However, since the contribution of this paper is constrained to the numerical reasoning modules, it would be nice if this was connected better to very similar work in numerical reasoning for other tasks that don't mix tabular and textual data. Alternatively, if there is something about the mixed tabular + textual domain that requires significantly different methods of program induction, the paper should make that explicit.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work extends the MT2NET by replacing the LSTM decoder with a non-autoregressive model to address the problem of exposure bias for hybrid tabular-textual question-answering tasks. The experimental results on the MultiHiertt dataset show that the proposed model outperforms the MT2NET by a significant margin. It also speeds up the inference time because the program tuples can be generated in parallel and the number of decoding steps is independent of the length of an entire program used to produce the answers.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

(1) The reported experimental results show that a state-of-the-art was achieved on the MultiHiertt dataset created for hybrid tabular-textual question answering by using a non-autoregressive decoder.

(2) The model with the non-autoregressive decoder can significantly speed up the inference time by about 21x, compared to an LSTM-based decoder. 

Weakness: 

(1) The proposed framework uses the same encoder, fact retriever, question type classifier, and span extractor as the MT2NET. The only difference between this work and the MT2NET is to replace the LSTM decoder with a non-autoregressive one. The novelty seems a bit insufficient.

(2) Only a single dataset was used to evaluate the performance of models.

(3) The scores of exact matching (EM) and the numeracy-focused F1 were not reported separately for two types of questions (i.e., numerical reasoning and span extraction). Therefore, it is unclear how the non-autoregressive decoder impacts the performance of answering questions where the decoder is required.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is generally well-organized and easy to follow. However, the novelty seems a bit insufficient because the proposed framework uses most of the modules that were included in the MT2NET.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a non-autoregressive program generation framework, which extends the MT2NET by replacing the LSTM decoder with a non-autoregressive one. The experimental results on the MultiHiertt dataset demonstrate that the implemented model with this framework can improve the performance for hybrid tabular-textual question-answering tasks while substantially reducing the inference time.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new non-autoregressive program generation framework based on MT2Net. The paper uses a length predictor, a soft-masking operand extractor, and a set of modules for the program generation of all steps. The model is then optimized with objectives including generation results, predicted length, operand probability, operator probability, and order probability. The author compared the model against three baselines. The paper also did speed analysis and performance analysis. It contains a case study and an ablation study over different hyperparameters.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength  
1. The paper proposes a new non-autoregressive program generation framework based on MT2Net and achieves the best results over all other baselines. The proposed method is more robust regarding increasing numbers of numerical reasoning steps. The paper provides several generation results as a case study in Appendix. The authors also provide an ablation study over different hyperparameters. 

2. The figures in the paper are clear and easy to follow. 

Weaknesses
1. The experiment section is not well written. In the section, the paper fails to explain the detailed reason behind the proposed method's performance increase. The paper also fails to include any qualitative analysis to show the effectiveness of each component. Most of the sentences in the section just repeat the table results. The paper lacks an in-depth analysis of the model's failure case.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The paper provides part of the training details in section 4.1. However, the code is missing from the submission making readers hard to reproduce the results. 

2. Most parts of the proposed model are based on MT2Net. The model only modifies the last step of generation. Moreover, the contributions of each newly added component are unclear. Overall, the model is a little bit incremental.

3. The experiment section is incomplete and lacks in-depth analysis.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the paper proposes an interesting non-autoregressive program generation model for hybrid tabular-textual question answering. However, the experiment and analysis section is not comprehensive and still has space to improve.

content.title: NAPG: Non-Autoregressive Program Generation for Hybrid Tabular-Textual Question Answering
content.TL;DR: We present a non-autoregressive program generation model for the numerical reasoning of hybrid question answering to address the exposure bias issue of autoregressive generation and to boost the decoding speed.
content.abstract: Hybrid tabular-textual question answering (QA) requires reasoning from heterogeneous information, and the types of reasoning are mainly divided into numerical reasoning and span extraction. The current numerical reasoning method uses LSTM to autoregressively decode program sequences, and each decoding step produces either an operator or an operand. However, the step-by-step decoding suffers from exposure bias, and the accuracy of program generation drops sharply with progressive decoding. In this paper, we propose a non-autoregressive program generation framework, which facilitates program generation in parallel. Our framework, which independently generates complete program tuples containing both operators and operands, can significantly boost the speed of program generation while addressing the error accumulation issue. Our experiments on the MultiHiertt dataset shows that our model can bring about large improvements (+7.97 EM and +6.38 F1 points) over the strong baseline, establishing the new state-of-the-art performance, while being much faster (~21x) in program generation. The performance drop of our method is also significantly smaller than the baseline with increasing numbers of numerical reasoning steps.
